title: The Grant
subtitle: Monday 4 to Friday 8 July 1881: Two Fourths of July, Wire on the Springs, a Junta in the Sala and a Cairn That Walked

setting.name: Santa Teresita, the commons, the Ojo del Gato and the Cerro Colorado, the first week of July
setting.description: The week the Company shows what it wants. On the Fourth of July Paragon holds a barbecue for the Progress ticket, and the first stolen notes cross the Silver Rail's bar. On Tuesday the Company's handbills go up in Plata Vieja promising the unpaid miners an advance on their wages, on election day, at the Company store, and the same morning its fence crew starts stringing wire round the Ojo del Gato springs, guarded by two of the men who robbed the coach. On Wednesday night the grant's vecinos meet in Don Fermín Lucero's sala to decide whether to take the Company's offer for the commons. On Thursday the Committee's riders come for the boy. Behind all of it is the land: the commons, the springs, the acequia, the Cerro Colorado cairn and a paper of 1768 that one widow has kept hidden for two years.
setting.atmosphere: The hottest week of the summer, until Thursday. The commons are gold grass and grey chamisa, with dust devils walking across the llano and sheep in long dusty bands moving to water. At the Ojo del Gato the springs come up under cottonwoods into stone tanks older than the republic, and the ring of a post maul carries a mile. The plaza is shade and whitewash. At night there are farolitos in the windows for the President, whom nobody here has met. Paragon on the Fourth is bunting, fireworks, a spitted steer and a brass band, and men who were strangers a week ago drinking to the county's future. On Thursday afternoon the first storm of the season comes over the Sierra Prieta like a wall: thunder, the smell of wet creosote, and a flash flood down an arroyo that was dry an hour before. The vecinos come out of their doors to stand in the rain.

keyLocations.name: Rufina Sedillo's sheep camp
keyLocations.description: Three miles west of the Ojo del Gato, in a fold of the hills: a stone house of two rooms built by Rufina's husband's grandfather, a brush ramada, a stone corral for two thousand sheep, a well, a pole pen for the goats, and three herders and their dogs. Tiburcio Archibeque has been hiding here since Thursday night, in the loft over the storeroom. Rufina has told the herders she will skin anyone who talks.
features: The storeroom loft, reached by a notched pole, where Tiburcio sleeps with an old cap-and-ball pistol he doesn't know how to load
The stone corral, chest-high, with a single gate and two thousand sheep inside it at night
The house's thick adobe wall beside the fireplace, with a small niche where a saint stood until 1879
A view east across the llano to the springs, where on Tuesday morning the Company's tents go up
encounters: Tiburcio Archibeque, who will shoot at the first stranger who comes up the loft pole unless someone he knows calls to him first
The Committee's riders on Thursday 7 July (see act 3)
secrets: CLUE A5 (core once Tiburcio trusts the party; Persuasion DC 13, automatic if Nicanor, Rufina or Celestino is with them): his story. On Monday 27 June at the Ojo del Gato a red-haired Texan who called himself Lige offered him $20 to guide four horse buyers over the old sheep trail to the Cañoncito. He held their horses in the arroyo below the Puerto de Piedra and thought they were waiting for someone. Then the shot, the shouting, and he looked over the bank and saw the messenger fall. He ran. He knows all four faces: Lige, the tall fair one called Cade with the long rifle, a dark one who spoke Spanish 'like a Texan priest', and a heavy one called Hob. 'They told me if I talked, my mother.'

CLUE B3 (Persuasion DC 12 with the old herder at the springs, Don Crispín Maestas, Don Policarpio's brother, who doesn't like Texans or the Company): he saw the red-haired Texan talking to Tiburcio at the spring on the 27th and saw money change hands. He'll swear to it. He'll also say that the same red-haired Texan is now guarding the Company's fence.

CLUE E5 (Rufina gives it only to someone she trusts with her family's honour; Insight DC 15 to see that the niche wall has been replastered and that she watches anyone who goes near it): behind the niche, in an oilcloth and a tin box, is the original act of possession of the Merced de Santa Teresita, 1768. Four leaves of rag paper in a clerk's hand, with the alcalde's rubric. It names the twenty-four families and gives them 'los pastos, aguas, montes y abrevaderos, en común para todos', the pastures, waters, woods and watering places, in common for all. Her husband Ramón hid it in 1879, when Don Fermín asked the comisión to lend the grant's papers to 'his lawyer'. The chest in the church has only an 1846 copy. Rufina has told no one, because it means saying that her husband did not trust the patrón.

Rufina's other secret, which she tells only if the party has earned it: in 1878 Ramón signed a letter, at Don Fermín's request, calling Don Fermín 'principal heir of the founder'. The Company has that letter. She thinks it may be what loses the grant. It isn't. Licenciado Montaño can explain that a courtesy to a patrón is not a deed. But it is why she is so angry with everyone.

keyLocations.name: The Ojo del Gato springs and the Company's fence
keyLocations.description: Fourteen miles south-west of the plaza: six springs rising under old cottonwoods into stone tanks, the grant's best water, where the sheep of half the commons drink. Ludlow's station is here, a little adobe with a corral on the Plata Vieja road. From Tuesday 5 July the Company's surveyor, Ozias Hornaday, has a tent here, and a fence crew of ten Paragon men is setting cedar posts and four strands of barbed wire round the springs. It is guarded by four 'Company range guards', two of them Shad Sorrel and Lige Tasker.
features: The fence line: a mile of new posts round the springs, with a painted board at the gap: PRIVATE PROPERTY — PARAGON T.&I. CO. — WATERING BY PERMIT, 5¢ A HEAD
Hornaday's tent: a drafting table, a theodolite, a Gunter's chain, a demijohn of whiskey and a tin map case
The stone tanks, where Don Crispín Maestas waters his sheep every morning, and has done for sixty years
Ludlow's little station, its keeper, and the road to Plata Vieja, where on Tuesday the Company's buckboard goes by with the handbills
encounters: The fence crew (ten Paragon men, non-combatants unless pushed) and four range guards: Shad Sorrel (Bandit Sharpshooter), Lige Tasker (Road Agent) and two Hired Guns
Thirty vaqueros and herders of the commons, armed, who mean to cut the fence on Wednesday night unless someone gives them a better idea
secrets: CLUE E2 (Investigation DC 13 to find it in the map case; Stealth DC 14 to get into the tent while Hornaday is at the tanks, or Persuasion or whiskey with Hornaday himself, who is lonely and drinks): the plat of 'Paragon South Addition and Rio Seco Irrigation District'. Lots, streets, a reservoir and a dam laid over the plaza's own irrigated fields, with the acequia madre's headgate marked 'to be acquired'. Every vecino's strip is drawn under a numbered lot. A Back East character or anyone who reads plats sees at once that the Company means to take the water, and that without the water the fields are worth nothing.

Shad Sorrel and Lige Tasker are two of the four robbers. Tiburcio knows both faces. Any passenger who heard the Spanish at the Puerto de Piedra can, with Insight DC 12, hear Sorrel's Spanish again when he shouts at Don Crispín's sheep: the same Texas Spanish, the same dropped r's (CLUE A2). The guards are bold because they believe the boy will be hanged before he can say anything.

Hornaday, drunk, says that the Cerro Colorado corner 'had to be adjusted to the true line' on Mr. Coldiron's instruction, and that it was 'a mile and a half out', in the Company's favour. He knows it was wrong and is ashamed of it (see the Cerro Colorado, E4).

If the vaqueros cut the fence on Wednesday night, Sorrel and Tasker are waiting, and the Company has its excuse: 'Mexican fence-cutters' is in the Paragon Pioneer by Friday and Constable Ebner has twenty more men. The fence can be beaten in better ways: Hornaday's own confession, a writ from the district court, or the junta's vote.

keyLocations.name: Don Fermín Lucero's house and sala
keyLocations.description: The biggest house on the plaza: a double square of adobe rooms round two courtyards, a hundred-foot portal on the plaza side, a private chapel, stables, storerooms and the sala, a long whitewashed room with vigas, a wooden floor, mirrors from St. Louis and portraits of the Lucero dead. It is where the plaza dances, and on Wednesday 6 July it is where the grant's junta meets. Don Fermín owns sixty thousand sheep, many of them out on partido with forty families, and the house is full of people who owe him something.
features: The sala: benches along the walls, a table at the end with Don Policarpio Maestas and the grant's comisión, candles, and a crucifix
Don Fermín's office off the first courtyard, with an iron safe, a writing desk and the Company's papers
The second courtyard, where the women gather during the junta and say what they think of it among themselves
Ascensión Lucero, nineteen, Don Fermín's granddaughter, who is in love with Rafael Candelaria and has opinions about everything
encounters: No combat. The junta: two hundred people, two speakers, a vote, and a room that can go either way
Constable Ebner (Crooked Sheriff) and Fenton Rusk, who arrive uninvited to 'observe' and are let in by Don Fermín because he will not shame a guest
secrets: CLUE E1 (Persuasion DC 14 with Don Fermín, who is proud of it; or Investigation in his office): his deed to the Company of 12 March 1881, conveying 'all the right, title and interest of the heirs of Ventura Lucero', with a clause in his own handwriting: 'excepting always the house lots, fields and waters of the vecinos of Santa Teresita, which are theirs'. He made the Company sign it. It is why he sleeps at night.

CLUE E3 (Investigation DC 12 to read the copy Licenciado Montaño sent Celestino; or Rusk, if he has a reason to show it): the Company's quiet-title petition, filed in May, asks the court to remove 'all occupants and trespassers' from 'the whole of the said grant, together with its waters'. It says nothing at all about any exception. A Back East character's Book Learning sees at once that the exception in Don Fermín's deed binds the Company only if someone makes it, and that the petition is written to make sure no one does.

Don Fermín's argument is the strongest one in the room, and he believes it. He has watched the Americans take grant after grant, he says, by lawyers and taxes and surveys, and he will not let Santa Teresita lose everything for the sake of the commons when it can save its houses and fields. He sold the Lucero claim so that a Lucero's signature would protect the fields, and so that the Company would have to deal with him instead of with lawyers. Show him E2 and E3 together, and he sees that the Company has used his signature to take exactly what he sold it to protect. Then he breaks, publicly, in his own sala (see the junta).

Venancio Chávez, the plaza's precinct boss, is at the junta counting heads. He knows to within ten how the room will vote and how the county will. He also owes the Paragon Mercantile $600 on a note the Company bought in June, and on Tuesday Rusk sent him a friendly letter about it. He does not tell anyone.

keyLocations.name: Paragon on the Fourth of July
keyLocations.description: The Company's town at its best: bunting on every false front, a spitted steer and kegs of beer on the vacant courthouse block, the brass band, a platform with Coldiron, Rusk, Don Fermín (who has come because he promised to, and is unhappy), the Pioneer's editor and a visiting territorial politician. There are races, a shooting match, fireworks at dark and free beer all day. Everything is paid for by the Committee. Its money comes from Rusk.
features: The beer kegs and the Silver Rail's bar, where the Committee's money is paid over in new $10 and $5 notes
The speakers' platform with its bunting, and the courthouse board: SITE OF THE RIO SECO COUNTY COURTHOUSE
The shooting match at the depot, $20 to the winner, where Cade Rendell shoots and wins, and offers to shoot anyone for a hundred
Victoriano Romero's section gang, who have the day off and are watching it all from the bunkhouse steps
encounters: Cade Rendell (Fast Gun) at the shooting match, who will take a showdown with anyone who has a name, if there is a crowd, and only then
A drunk crowd (Saloon Brawlers and Drunk Cowboys) that turns ugly if anyone from the plaza is recognised, and uglier when the fireworks start
secrets: CLUE C2 (core, automatic for anyone who has the schedule and handles the money): the change across the Silver Rail's bar, the purse for the shooting match, and the beer money are new Bank of the Rio Abajo notes in the stolen ranges. The barkeep says the Committee paid for the beer this morning 'in a stack like a brick'. The Committee's treasurer says Mr. Rusk advanced it.

Rendell wins the shooting match with an ivory-handled Army revolver. He does not bring the buffalo rifle to town. A Gunslinger or Scout watching him shoot (Perception DC 13) sees that he reads distance and wind like a man who has shot a great deal at long range. If Royal Penhallow is played, Rendell greets him by name in front of the crowd, as an old friend. That puts Royal on the Committee's suspicion list at once.

Theodora Quayle, if played, sees the depot operator Uriah Quist hand Rusk a sheaf of message copies in the Silver Rail's back hall. Paragon's telegraph is the Company's ear (CLUE C3's thread: she now remembers the Albuquerque wire of 20 June. 'ENVELOPES FOUR HUNDRED PRINTED AS ORDERED SHIP PARAGON FIRST WEEK JULY'. The printer was Cazenove & Son, Railroad Avenue.)

Don Fermín, on the platform, is introduced as 'our next probate judge' and speaks for two minutes, in Spanish, about the future of the county and the honour of his family. The Anglo crowd cheers what it doesn't understand. Insight DC 12 for anyone who understands him: he is speaking to his own people, not to Paragon, and he sounds like a man trying to convince himself.

keyLocations.name: The Cerro Colorado
keyLocations.description: A red sandstone hill at the grant's north-west corner, twenty miles from the plaza and eight from Paragon, where the commons meet the pasture of Laguna Pueblo. On its shoulder an old stone cairn, a mojonera, marked the corner, and both communities walked to it in 1856 with their officers and their witnesses and agreed it. In June the Company's surveyor moved it a mile and a half west. That put Paragon's two new wells, and a long strip of Laguna's pasture, inside the 'Lucero private grant'.
features: The old footing on the hill's shoulder: a square of bare ground without lichen, and the old stones rolled into the arroyo below
The new cairn on a rise a mile and a half west, of fresh-broken stone, with the surveyor's stake beside it: P.T.&I. CO. — N.W. COR. — LUCERO GRANT
Paragon's two new wells and windmills, visible from the hill, inside the new line
Laguna's sheep and a herder's camp, now on the Company's side of a line nobody told them about
encounters: No set combat. Victoriano Romero and two men of Laguna, who meet the party here on Thursday by arrangement
If the party comes with Company men or is followed, two range guards (Hired Gun) who tell everyone, Laguna included, to get off Company land
secrets: CLUE E4 (core once Victoriano shows them; Survival or Investigation DC 12 to read the footing and the new stones for themselves): the old corner stood on the shoulder of the hill. The old stones are in the arroyo, lichened on one side and clean on the other, where they lay for a century. The new cairn's stones were broken this spring. Victoriano has a copy of the 1856 boundary agreement in Spanish, signed by Laguna's governor of that day and Santa Teresita's comisión, which names the Cerro Colorado and 'its shoulder that looks east'.

Victoriano's interest is Laguna's, and he says so plainly. The pueblo's governor and council sent him because the moved corner takes Laguna pasture, and the pueblo's lawyer in Santa Fe will protest it to the Surveyor General. He wants witnesses who are neither of the pueblo nor of the plaza to see the footing and swear to it. He is not on the plaza's side in the election, which is not Laguna's business, and he says so: 'When this is finished Don Policarpio and our governor will go back to arguing about the same mile of pasture they have argued about since my grandfather's time. That is our business. This is not.'

Victoriano also has the last piece of B4 if he didn't give it before: the saddlebags that Hob Linnet brought in on the night of 1 July went from the hotel to the Mercantile's back door, carried by Fenton Rusk himself.

If the party helps Victoriano, by swearing to the footing, getting Hornaday's admission, or carrying Laguna's protest to Albuquerque with their own papers in st-scenario-004, Laguna's attitude to the party becomes trusting. In st-scenario-004 his section gang can stop a train, or not stop it, and the pueblo's horse herd is twenty miles from the Puerco crossing.

synopsis: The week the land comes into it. The party has the boy, or must find him before the Committee does: Tiburcio Archibeque is in Rufina Sedillo's loft at her sheep camp, and he saw all four robbers' faces. On the Fourth of July Paragon holds a barbecue for the Progress ticket and pays for the beer with stolen notes, and Cade Rendell wins the shooting match and offers a showdown to anyone with a name. On Tuesday Thomasina Bevan rides down from Plata Vieja with a Company handbill. The unpaid miners are promised an advance on their June wages, at the Paragon Mercantile, on election day only. The same morning the Company starts fencing the Ojo del Gato springs, and two of its four range guards are robbers from the Puerto de Piedra. The vaqueros mean to cut the wire, which is exactly what the Company wants them to do. On Wednesday night the grant's junta meets in Don Fermín Lucero's sala. Don Fermín argues, honestly, that the vecinos should take the Company's offer and save their houses and fields. Celestino Trujillo argues, less wisely, that he has sold them. Jethro Petree, coming apart, tries to give his gold back to Rusk and is told that Mr. Rendell sends his regards. On Thursday the party rides to the Cerro Colorado with Victoriano Romero of Laguna to see a boundary cairn that walked a mile and a half, and the Committee's riders, led by one of the robbers, come for the boy at the sheep camp, just as the first storm of the season breaks. Rufina has a paper in her wall that can save the grant, if she can bring herself to say why it is there. On Friday Cyprian Ludlow sells the Puerco station to the Company to pay the bank.
hook: Monday 4 July, early, at the plaza. Rufina Sedillo rides in on a grey mule with a rifle across the saddle and asks for the party by name, or by description. 'You are the ones who brought the messenger home. They say you looked at the ground before you looked at the people. Come with me. Bring nobody else.' If the party already has Tiburcio, it is Celestino who comes instead, with Licenciado Montaño's letter in his hand and a question: 'The junta is on Wednesday. Don Fermín wants us to sell the commons to the men who did this. Will you come and tell them what you saw?'

conclusions.conclusion: C. The Company paid for it
clues: C2: stolen notes paying for the beer and the shooting match (Paragon, the Fourth)
C3: the Albuquerque wire about four hundred envelopes (Theodora, the depot)
C4 and F2: Jethro's double eagles (the plaza store, Doña Luz)
C6: Jethro's word that Rusk paid him (the corrals, the church)
B4: Rusk carried Linnet's saddlebags to the Mercantile (Victoriano)

conclusions.conclusion: D. The Company means to buy the election
clues: D1: the handbill, an advance on wages payable in Paragon on election day (Thomasina, Plata Vieja)
The beer and the band, paid for by the Committee in stolen notes (Paragon)
Rusk's letter to Venancio Chávez about his note (Venancio, if he trusts the party)

conclusions.conclusion: E. The commons are the prize, and Don Fermín has been deceived
clues: E1: Don Fermín's deed with its exception (his office)
E2: the plat laying lots over the plaza's fields and taking the acequia (Hornaday's tent)
E3: the petition to remove 'all occupants' from the whole grant (Montaño's copy)
E4: the moved cairn at the Cerro Colorado (Victoriano, Hornaday)
E5: the act of possession, 'in common for all' (Rufina's wall)

acts.title: Monday and Tuesday: Two Fourths of July
acts.description: The party finds the boy, sees the Company's money spent in public, and learns what the Company means to do with the miners. These three scenes can come in any order. A party that has Tiburcio from st-scenario-001 starts with the barbecue. A party that doesn't must find him first, and Rufina's arrival on Monday morning is the GM's way of making sure they can.
objectives: Find Tiburcio and earn his story, and decide where he is safest
See the stolen notes spent in Paragon, and who is spending them
Learn what the handbill means for the miners and the election
Do not get killed in a showdown with Cade Rendell in front of a crowd

scenes.name: The Boy in the Loft
scenes.description: Rufina's sheep camp. Tiburcio is seventeen, slight, quick, the best rider on the plaza, and he has not slept since Thursday. He has an old cap-and-ball pistol that isn't loaded. He will talk to Nicanor or Rufina at once and to anyone else only when they have convinced him they are not bounty hunters. His story is the robbery from the other side. The scene's question is what to do with him. The plaza's jail is the obvious place and the worst, because the Committee will come for it. The sheep camp is safe until Thursday. Nobody knows about the Cañoncito but the robbers. Albuquerque is seventy miles off, through country the Committee watches.
scenes.readAloud: The camp is a stone house the colour of the hill, with a ramada of juniper brush, a corral full of sheep and dust, two dogs who come at you silently, and a woman's voice that stops them with one word. Rufina Sedillo swings down from the mule, pushes back her hat and looks at you for a long moment before she says anything at all. Then she calls toward the storeroom, softly, 'Tiburcio. Mijo. They're here. Come down.' Nothing. Then a scrape in the loft above the storeroom door and a boy's voice, high and cracking: 'Who? Who are they? Tía, who?' A pistol barrel comes out between the poles of the loft, shaking so badly you can hear it knock against the wood.

skillChecks.success: He comes down. He tells it all (CLUE A5): Lige at the spring, the $20, the four faces, the long rifle, the messenger falling, the sombrero he lost, and 'if you talk, your mother'. He gives you names and descriptions: Lige the red-haired one, Cade the tall fair one with the long rifle, a dark one who spoke Spanish 'like a Texan priest', and a heavy one called Hob. (Automatic with Nicanor, Rufina or Celestino present.)
skillChecks.failure: He won't come down. Rufina sends you outside, and it takes an hour and a bowl of her posole before he will speak to you at all, and then only through her.

skillChecks.success: He is telling the truth, all of it, and he's ashamed of the $20 more than he is afraid of the rope. He also thinks his uncle Celestino will never forgive him. Telling him that he is the most important witness in the county does more for him than any kindness.
skillChecks.failure: He is frightened, and frightened people lie. You can't tell which this is.

skillChecks.success: He hasn't eaten or slept properly in four days and has a cut on his hand gone red. You clean it, make him eat and make him sleep. He sleeps for fourteen hours, and wakes up able to think. His testimony will be much better for it.
skillChecks.failure: He's exhausted and feverish, and his story keeps sliding about. He'll need a day before he can tell it straight.

scenes.name: The Barbecue
scenes.description: Paragon on the Fourth: bunting, beer, a steer on a spit, races, the band, the platform speeches, the shooting match at the depot and fireworks at dark. A party that comes from the plaza is noticed, and a party with the plaza's coach horses is recognised. The stolen notes are everywhere, in the beer money and the purse and the Silver Rail's till. Rendell wins the shooting match and offers to shoot anyone for a hundred dollars, and with a crowd round him he will make it a showdown if anyone gives him a reason. Rusk is on the platform, delighted to see the party, and introduces them to Don Fermín.
scenes.readAloud: Paragon has painted itself red, white and blue. Bunting on every false front, a flag on the water tank, the band in its borrowed uniforms playing 'Hail, Columbia' for the third time, and on the vacant block marked SITE OF THE RIO SECO COUNTY COURTHOUSE a whole steer turning on a spit over a trench of coals, with a dozen kegs of beer on trestles and a sign: COMPLIMENTS OF THE PARAGON CITIZENS' COMMITTEE. VOTE PROGRESS. On the platform under the bunting sit a lean handsome man in a white suit, a plump pleasant one in a straw boater, and between them a grey-bearded Hispano gentleman in a black coat and a silver-buckled hat, sitting very straight, who looks as if he would rather be anywhere else on earth. At the depot a rifle cracks, and the crowd there cheers a tall fair man who lowers a pistol and says, quite softly, 'Anybody else?'

skillChecks.success: With the schedule in your hand, the money is easy. Your change at the Silver Rail, the notes the barkeep pays for kegs, and the shooting match's purse are new Bank of the Rio Abajo tens and fives in the stolen ranges (CLUE C2). The barkeep says the Committee paid him 'in a stack like a brick' this morning, and the Committee's treasurer, a hardware merchant, says Mr. Rusk advanced it. You can buy one or two of them back as evidence for a dollar each over face value.
skillChecks.failure: New notes everywhere, but without the numbers in front of you they're just money.

skillChecks.success: Rendell is not drunk, and he isn't here to celebrate. He's here to be seen. He wants a showdown in front of this crowd with someone whose name means something, so he can leave the territory famous. If anyone in the party has a name or a star, he is choosing between them now.
skillChecks.failure: A Texan showing off. There's one at every Fourth of July in the West.

skillChecks.success: Rusk introduces you to Don Fermín, who is courteous and unhappy. If you speak to him in Spanish, or speak to him as an equal rather than a curiosity, he tells you quietly that he is here because he gave his word, that he is not ashamed of the bargain he made, and that if you have something to say against the Company you should say it at the junta on Wednesday, in his house, to his people. 'Not here. Here they do not listen.'
skillChecks.failure: Rusk introduces you to Don Fermín as 'the plaza's new friends'. The old man bows, and is cold.

scenes.name: The Handbill
scenes.description: Tuesday 5 July. Thomasina Bevan rides down from Plata Vieja on a borrowed mule with a handbill in her pocket, looking for whoever she has heard is asking questions about the payroll. If Zadok Morgenstern is played, he comes with her, or sent her. The miners have not been paid. Hamish Gow, the mine superintendent, has no money until the bank and the express company settle, which will take weeks. The Company store has stopped giving credit. And this morning the Company's buckboard went up the road with the handbills. The miners are angry, and Thomasina is trying to keep them from doing something stupid, either way.
scenes.readAloud: She is a small square woman in a black bonnet and a grey dust-coat, sitting a mule as if it had personally offended her, and she gets down without waiting for anyone to help her. 'Mrs. Bevan,' she says. 'From Plata Vieja. I keep the school. I'm told you are the people who found that the bandits came out of Paragon and not off the plaza.' She takes a folded paper from her coat and holds it out. It's a printed handbill, black type on yellow: MINERS OF PLATA VIEJA! The PARAGON MERCANTILE, as a PUBLIC SERVICE, will ADVANCE your JUNE WAGES, stolen by MEXICAN BANDITS, at its PARAGON STORE, on TUESDAY 12 JULY ONLY. Free conveyance by Company wagons. Refreshments. VOTE PROGRESS. 'Three hundred and eighty men,' Thomasina says, 'with their children going hungry. Tell me where a store finds four thousand dollars in cash on a week's notice, and why it can only give it to them in Paragon on election day.'

skillChecks.success: The arithmetic is the clue, and Thomasina has already done half of it. Paying the miners on election day in Paragon puts all three hundred and eighty of them in Paragon's precinct, citizens or not, voting Progress in front of the Company's judges (CLUE D1). Venancio Chávez, or anyone who has run an election, can tell you what that does to the county: it moves about four hundred votes.
skillChecks.failure: It looks like charity with a ticket attached. That's not unusual in a territorial election.

skillChecks.success: Thomasina trusts you. She tells you the miners' committee meets on Saturday night in her schoolroom, and that if anyone can show them that the Company's 'advance' is their own stolen pay, they will go home on election day and vote where they live. She can get you into the meeting. She also tells you, because she believes in plain dealing, that Hamish Gow gave Celestino Trujillo $300 for the People's ticket on 15 June. If the Company prints it before you do, the miners will think the plaza bought them first.
skillChecks.failure: Thomasina thanks you and says she will make up her own mind, as she always does.

skillChecks.success: The handbill's printer's line, in tiny type at the foot: CAZENOVE & SON, PRINTERS, RAILROAD AVE., ALBUQUERQUE. If Theodora Quayle is played, that is the name she remembers from the 20 June wire about four hundred envelopes (CLUE C3). Otherwise, it is a name to ask about in Albuquerque or at the Mercantile.
skillChecks.failure: A Company handbill on cheap yellow paper. You can't tell anything more from it.

encounters: Cade Rendell (Fast Gun) at the shooting match: a showdown in the street if anyone accepts or is shamed into it (frontier.json showdowns). He will not fight any other way in town. If he loses the stare-down he backs off with a laugh, and the town notices
A drunk crowd at the fireworks (two Saloon Brawlers and three Drunk Cowboys) that recognises the plaza's people. Brawling rules; nobody means to kill anybody, until someone draws

acts.title: Tuesday and Wednesday: Wire on the Springs
acts.description: The fence goes up round the Ojo del Gato, and the plaza decides what to do about the commons. The fence is a provocation built to be cut. Two of the robbers guard it, and the Company wants the vaqueros to come at it in the dark so it can call them fence-cutters and bandits in the same sentence. The junta on Wednesday night is the scenario's centre. Two hundred people in Don Fermín's sala decide whether to take the Company's offer, and the party can speak if invited. Between the two is Jethro Petree, who can't bear it any more.
objectives: Find the plat in Hornaday's tent, and see the faces of the Company's range guards
Keep the vaqueros from cutting the fence into the Company's hands
Speak at the junta, if invited, and put the evidence in front of Don Fermín
Hear Jethro Petree's confession, and protect him and Doña Luz afterwards

scenes.name: The Fence
scenes.description: The Ojo del Gato on Tuesday or Wednesday. Ten Paragon men setting cedar posts, four range guards with rifles, Hornaday's tent, a painted board at the gap: WATERING BY PERMIT. Don Crispín Maestas, seventy, waters his sheep at the stone tanks as he has every morning for sixty years and tells the guards in Spanish what he thinks of them. Sorrel answers in his Texas Spanish, and anyone who was on the coach hears the voice. Thirty vaqueros are waiting in the hills to cut the wire on Wednesday night. Rufina is with them and Nicanor wants to be.
scenes.readAloud: You hear it from a mile off across the llano in the still morning: the thud of a post maul, steady as a heartbeat, and the twang of wire being stretched. Then you see it, a line of raw cedar posts marching round the cottonwoods at the springs, four strands of barbed wire glittering in the sun, a white tent, a wagon, a dozen men in shirtsleeves, and four more on horses with rifles across their saddles, sitting where they can see everything. At the stone tanks an old man in a straw hat and a white shirt is watering his sheep as if none of it were there, and he is talking, loudly, to the nearest rider. The rider is dark, lean, sunburned, and he answers in Spanish, lazily, and laughs. And the sound of his voice goes through you like cold water, because you have heard it before, from the rocks above a dead man.

skillChecks.success: That's the voice from the Puerto de Piedra: the dropped r's, the Texas words (CLUE A2, again). The red-haired guard beside him rides like the man who held the rifle on the north outcrop. They are two of the robbers, guarding the Company's fence in broad daylight, and they aren't afraid of being seen. Somebody has told them the boy will hang first.
skillChecks.failure: Range guards. The Company has hired some hard men.

skillChecks.success: You get into Hornaday's tent while he is down at the tanks arguing with Don Crispín. In the tin map case is the plat of Paragon South Addition and Rio Seco Irrigation District: lots over the plaza's fields and the acequia's headgate 'to be acquired' (CLUE E2). You can take it or copy it. A copy is safer. If it is missed, Hornaday will be blamed, and he will be frightened enough to talk.
skillChecks.failure: Hornaday comes back early. He doesn't shout. He looks at you, at the map case, and says, 'I'd go, if I were you, before those boys on the horses notice.' He's a frightened man, and he'll remember that you got as far as the case.

skillChecks.success: You talk the vaqueros out of cutting the wire on Wednesday night. Show them the plat, or tell them who the guards are, or simply tell Rufina that the Company wants them to do it. They hold off until after the junta. Reputation in Santa Teresita +1, and the Company loses its 'Mexican fence-cutters' story.
skillChecks.failure: They will cut it on Wednesday night after the junta, whatever the junta says. If the party isn't with them, Sorrel and Tasker ambush them at the wire, and two vaqueros are shot. The Pioneer prints 'MEXICAN FENCE-CUTTERS REPULSED' on Friday.

scenes.name: The Junta
scenes.description: Wednesday night in Don Fermín's sala. Two hundred people: the vecinos of the plaza and Los Ranchitos, the herders, the women along the walls and in the courtyard doors, Don Policarpio Maestas and the comisión at the table, Venancio Chávez counting heads by the door, and Rusk and Ebner as uninvited observers. Don Fermín speaks first, and well. Take the Company's offer: deeds to the house lots and fields, $20 a family for their rights in the commons, grazing by permit at five cents a head. Save what can be saved. Celestino answers, too angrily, and calls him a vendido. The room is split. Strangers may speak only if someone on the comisión invites them. If the party puts the plat (E2) and the petition (E3) in front of Don Fermín, in his own sala, with the deed (E1) beside them, he reads them in silence. Then he turns to Rusk and asks him to leave his house. That is the turning of the election, and the party should see it happen.
scenes.readAloud: The sala is long and white and full of candles, and every bench and doorway and inch of wall is people: men in their best black coats, herders smelling of sheep and woodsmoke, women in rebozos along the walls with children asleep against them, girls in the courtyard doorway. At the table at the end, under the crucifix and a portrait of a stern man in a Spanish officer's coat, sits a very old man with white hair to his collar, Don Policarpio Maestas, who rings a little brass bell for silence. He gets it. Then Don Fermín Lucero rises from his chair by the table, grey and straight, puts one hand flat on the table and begins to speak, in Spanish, slowly. 'Compadres. I have watched the Americans take the land of every grant from the Rio Arriba to the Mesilla. By lawyers. By taxes. By surveys. By waiting. I will not let them take everything from us. I have made a bargain to keep our houses and our fields. I ask you to make it with me.' Nobody moves. By the door, a plump man in a straw boater listens with his head on one side, and smiles.

skillChecks.success: Invited to speak, you put the deed, the plat and the petition in front of Don Fermín, in that order, and say what they mean, plainly and with respect for him in his own house. He reads them in silence. Then he looks up at Rusk and says, in English, very quietly, 'You will leave my house.' He tears up the Company's offer, and his partidarios watch him do it. Don Fermín withdraws from the Progress ticket on Thursday, and most of his 120 votes go to the People's ticket or stay home (campaignRules, The Vote). Reputation in Santa Teresita +2. (Advantage if Celestino has first apologised to him for 'vendido', which he will do if the party asks him to.)
skillChecks.failure: Without the papers, or if they are thrown at him, Don Fermín will not be shamed in his own sala by strangers. He stands by his bargain and the junta splits. Most of his people vote Progress on the 12th, and the vecinos go home divided. He may still be turned later, privately, with the papers, but not in front of everyone.

skillChecks.success: Venancio Chávez, by the door, isn't counting heads for the People's ticket the way he usually does. He keeps looking at Rusk, and every time Rusk smiles at him he looks away. Something is wrong between them. In private he will admit the $600 note and Rusk's letter, if you get him alone and show him that you aren't judging him.
skillChecks.failure: The plaza's precinct boss, doing what precinct bosses do.

skillChecks.success: If Rufina is with the party, help her speak. Women do not usually speak at the junta, though some have, and she has never done it. She stands up at the wall and says that her sheep will die if the springs are fenced, and so will everyone else's, and that grazing by permit means grazing at the Company's pleasure. The herders stamp their feet. The room is with her.
skillChecks.failure: Rufina starts to speak and is told, kindly, by an old man, to sit down. She does, white with anger, and leaves before the end.

scenes.name: Doña Luz's Double Eagle
scenes.description: Jethro Petree can't bear it any more. On Wednesday he rode to Paragon and tried to give Rusk his gold back. Rusk laughed, told him to keep it, and said that Mr. Rendell sent his regards. Jethro understood. He came home, and on Wednesday night or Thursday morning he is sitting on the coach's box in the dark corral, with a bottle and a revolver. If the party was kind to him at the Puerco station, he comes to them. If not, Rafael brings them, or Doña Luz does, because the plaza is talking about the double eagle she spent at the store. The confession is a scene to play slowly. He'll say it once, to someone he trusts, and he'll say it again in court only if Doña Luz is safe.
scenes.readAloud: The corral is dark except for a lantern hung on the coach's brake handle, and the old man is sitting up on the box where he has sat for thirteen years, with the lines gathered in his hands as if the horses were there. There aren't any. La Doña stands with her pole on the ground and her doors open, smelling of leather and dust. There is a bottle on the seat beside him and a revolver in his lap. When he sees you he doesn't move. 'Lon used to sit there,' he says. 'Right there where the bottle is. Thirteen years and I never lost a sack. I want you to know that. Thirteen years.' His voice goes. 'They said nobody'd get hurt. They said the express was insured and it was only paper to them. I tied that rag in my head a hundred times before they ever tied it on the tree.'

skillChecks.success: He tells it (CLUE B6, C6): Rusk at the Paragon House on 24 June, the head driver's job on the buckboard line at $90 a month, $500 in gold and $100 down, the red rag, halting at the top of the grade, the padlock key. He didn't know about the rifle. He tried to give the money back today and Rusk said Mr. Rendell sent his regards. He has the buckboard line's letter offering him the job from 1 August in his coat (CLUE F3). He'll say it all to a judge if somebody can keep Luz safe.
skillChecks.failure: He says only, 'I stopped the team. I stopped the team,' over and over, and then that he's going to bed. In the morning he's gone, to Paragon, to try again with Rusk. Unless the party follows, he doesn't come back (see st-scenario-003).

skillChecks.success: The revolver in his lap is for himself, not for you. Take it from him gently and he lets you. If nobody notices it, he does nothing tonight, but the GM should know it is there.
skillChecks.failure: He's drunk and he's armed and he's grieving. You can't tell how dangerous that is, or to whom.

skillChecks.success: If you have no patience for him, you can frighten it out of him: the rag, the key, Rusk's name, the gold. It's all true. But he won't say it again to anyone else, and Rafael Candelaria, if he hears how you did it, will not forgive you quickly.
skillChecks.failure: He turns his face away and won't say another word. 'Hang me, then. Go on. I'd thank you.'

encounters: The fence: Shad Sorrel (Bandit Sharpshooter), Lige Tasker (Road Agent) and two range guards (Hired Gun), with the fence crew (non-combatants). A fight here in daylight gives the Company its 'Mexican bandits' story unless the party has the evidence ready to say why
If the vaqueros cut the fence on Wednesday night: Sorrel and Tasker waiting in the cottonwoods with two Hired Guns; the vaqueros (use Rustler stats) have numbers and no plan

acts.title: Thursday and Friday: The Corner of the Grant
acts.description: The boundary, the boy and the paper. On Thursday morning Victoriano Romero meets the party at the Cerro Colorado, as arranged, to show them a cairn that walked a mile and a half. On Thursday afternoon the Committee comes for Tiburcio at Rufina's camp, led by Lige Tasker, who wants the boy dead rather than tried. At about four the first storm of the season breaks over the Sierra Prieta. Afterwards, if the camp held and the party has earned it, Rufina takes down the plaster from the niche in her wall. On Friday, word comes from the plaza that Cyprian Ludlow has sold the Puerco station to the Company to pay the bank.
objectives: See the moved cairn with Victoriano Romero, and agree what each side will swear to
Hold the sheep camp, or get Tiburcio away from it, when the Committee comes
Earn Rufina's trust, and the act of possession
Keep everyone alive through the first flash flood of the season

scenes.name: The Cerro Colorado
scenes.description: Thursday morning at the grant's north-west corner. Victoriano Romero and two men of Laguna meet the party on the hill's shoulder, as he arranged by sending word through his section gang. He shows them the old footing and the new cairn, and his copy of the 1856 agreement. He asks them to swear to what they see, because their word comes from neither side. He is courteous, dry and precise. He does not ask for help in the election and does not offer any: it is not Laguna's business. He wants Laguna's corner back, and he is quite willing to work with the plaza to get it. Treat him and his companions exactly as seriously as Don Fermín.
scenes.readAloud: The Cerro Colorado stands up out of the llano like a great red loaf, bare and striped, with a crown of juniper and a long shoulder on its eastern side that catches the morning sun. Three men are waiting on the shoulder, their horses hobbled below. Victoriano Romero in his railroad cap and wool coat, and two older men in calico shirts and dark trousers with blankets rolled behind their saddles, who look at you with polite and complete reserve. Victoriano raises a hand. 'Good morning. You came. Good.' He walks you to a square of bare red ground on the shoulder, three paces across, with no lichen on it, and points down into the arroyo below, where a heap of grey stones lies in the sand. 'That was the corner. Our governor and the people of Santa Teresita walked to it in 1856 and agreed it, and put their names to a paper. Now look west.' A mile and a half off, on a low rise, there is a new cairn of raw broken stone with a white-painted stake beside it.

skillChecks.success: The old stones in the arroyo are lichened on one face and clean on the other, where they lay against each other for a century; they were pushed off the shoulder this spring. The new cairn's stones were broken with a hammer weeks ago. The stake reads P.T.&I. CO. — N.W. COR. — LUCERO GRANT. The new line puts Paragon's two new wells inside the Company's claim, and a long strip of Laguna's pasture, with a Laguna herder's camp on it, on the Company's side too (CLUE E4).
skillChecks.failure: Stones, a hill and a stake. You'll have to take Victoriano's word for it, which is worth something but not as much in court as your own.

skillChecks.success: Victoriano isn't here as anybody's ally. He is here as Laguna's representative, and he wants the party to understand exactly that. He is also, privately, angry: the Company's surveyor walked across Laguna pasture without asking anyone, and told the herder to move his sheep off 'Company land'. If the party treats that as seriously as the plaza's fields, he'll trust them.
skillChecks.failure: He's polite and careful, and you can't tell what he thinks of any of you.

skillChecks.success: You agree what each side will swear to and where. Victoriano will give his pueblo's protest to the party to carry with the plaza's papers to Albuquerque on 18 July, if they are going, along with his own sworn statement about the cairn, about the four riders on 27 June and about Rusk carrying Linnet's saddlebags (CLUE B4). Laguna's attitude to the party becomes trusting.
skillChecks.failure: Victoriano will send the pueblo's protest by its own lawyer in Santa Fe, in its own time. That's slower, and it doesn't help the plaza's case on the 18th.

scenes.name: Riders at the Sheep Camp
scenes.description: Thursday afternoon. A herder's boy talked at the Ojo del Gato, and the Committee knows where Tiburcio is. Lige Tasker leads Ebner's two hard men and six Committee riders, about ten guns, to Rufina's camp. The Committee men want to take the boy alive to Paragon, to hang him lawfully or otherwise. Tasker wants him shot 'resisting', because the boy has seen his face. The camp is a stone house, a stone corral and two thousand sheep. A rider coming in to warn the party (Rafael, a herder, or Ascensión Lucero on her grandfather's best horse) gives them half an hour. At about four the storm breaks: blinding rain, hail and thunder that can stampede the sheep through anything in their way.
scenes.readAloud: The herder's boy comes over the hill at a dead run on a sweating pony, shouting before he is in earshot, and behind him, three miles off across the llano, is a long brown smudge of dust with rifles winking in it. Behind them the sky over the Sierra Prieta has gone the colour of a bruise. A great white anvil of cloud is towering up out of it, flickering inside, and the first cold gust of wind comes across the grass and flattens it silver. The sheep in the corral begin to move, all together, the way water moves. Rufina Sedillo looks at the dust, at the sky, at the corral and at you, and says, 'Ten. Maybe twelve. And God is coming behind them.' Up in the loft, Tiburcio has begun to pray.

skillChecks.success: With Rufina's herders you open the corral at the right moment and send two thousand frightened sheep pouring out down the slope into the riders' faces as the hail hits (use combat.json stampedes at half damage; sheep are not longhorns, but horses hate them). The Committee's line breaks up in the rain. Tasker is left with whoever stays with him, and the Committee men are suddenly much less sure they want to die for a reward.
skillChecks.failure: The sheep break the wrong way, through the camp. Everyone has to find a wall, and two herders' dogs are lost. The Committee arrives in the confusion.

skillChecks.success: In the yard, in the rain, you tell the Committee men what you know: the factory shoes from their own livery, the Paragon cartridge box, the hotel register, and that the red-haired man leading them is one of the robbers. Tiburcio, if he is brave enough to stand in the doorway and say 'That's him, that's Lige', makes it certain. The Committee men turn on Tasker or ride away. Reputation in Paragon +1, which is the first time it has gone up.
skillChecks.failure: They don't believe you, or don't want to. It comes to guns.

skillChecks.success: You get Tiburcio out the back and up the arroyo before the riders reach the camp. You know, or Rufina does, that the arroyo will run in twenty minutes and that it is the one direction nobody will follow. You reach high ground just as the flood comes down behind you, a brown wall of water and juniper trunks, and the riders on the far side can only watch.
skillChecks.failure: You get out the back but misjudge the arroyo. The flood catches the last of you: DEX save DC 13 or 2d6 bludgeoning and swept fifty yards. You'll have to haul each other out.

scenes.name: The Wall
scenes.description: After the storm, at dusk, with the camp wet and battered and everyone alive, or not. If the party has earned it, by defending the boy, respecting her at the junta or treating her as the person in charge, Rufina takes a knife to the plaster in the niche beside her fireplace and brings out a tin box. Inside is the original act of possession of 1768. She tells them why it is there: her husband did not trust Don Fermín in 1879, and she has never dared say so. This scene is quiet, and it is the grant's heart. If the party has turned Don Fermín, she may give it to him, which is a reconciliation the plaza will talk about for fifty years.
scenes.readAloud: The rain has gone east, and the whole country smells of wet earth and creosote, and the arroyo below the camp is roaring brown. In the stone house a fire is going and everyone is wet. Rufina stands looking at the empty niche in the wall beside the fireplace, where a little painted saint stood until two years ago. Then she takes a knife from the table and cuts into the plaster, carefully, in a square. It comes away in pieces. Behind it is a hollow in the adobe, and in the hollow is a tin box wrapped in oilcloth. She takes it out and holds it a moment before she opens it. Inside are four folded sheets of brown rag paper, written close in an old clerk's hand, with a great looping rubric at the foot of the last. 'My Ramón put it there,' she says, 'the year Don Fermín asked to borrow the papers for his lawyer. He said, Rufina, a patrón is a patrón, but paper is paper. I never told anyone. It shames him that he did not trust a Lucero.' She holds it out. 'It does not shame me.'

skillChecks.success: It's the act of possession of the Merced de Santa Teresita, 14 May 1768. The alcalde of the district walked the boundaries with Ventura Lucero and the twenty-four families, named them all one by one, gave each its house lot and field, and gave them 'los pastos, aguas, montes y abrevaderos, en común para todos'. The Company's petition rests on Lucero's petition alone, and this answers it (CLUE E5). Book Learning or Spanish reads it in an hour. Licenciado Montaño must have it by 18 July.
skillChecks.failure: Old Spanish in a clerk's hand. It's plainly important and plainly the grant's, but you'll need Celestino or Don Policarpio to read it to you.

skillChecks.success: She is offering the party the most valuable thing in the county, and she's watching to see what they do with it. If they say it belongs to the grant and ask her where she wants it kept, she trusts them for good. If they put it in their own saddlebags without asking, she lets them, and never quite forgives it.
skillChecks.failure: She hands it over and says nothing more.

skillChecks.success: You suggest that Don Fermín see it, if he has broken with the Company. Rufina takes it to him herself on Friday. The old man reads it standing in his portal with his hat in his hand. Then he gives her his arm and walks her across the plaza to the church, where it goes into the comisión's chest in front of witnesses. The plaza is one again, for now. The People's party's attitude becomes trusting.
skillChecks.failure: Rufina won't let the paper go near a Lucero. It stays hidden until the party takes it to Albuquerque, and the plaza stays a little divided.

encounters: The sheep camp: Lige Tasker (Road Agent), two of Ebner's hard men (Hired Gun) and six Committee riders (Vigilante), in the open and then in a hailstorm; the stone house is full cover with loopholes, the corral wall half cover. The Committee men break when Tasker is down or exposed; Tasker fights to the end
The first flash flood of the season down the arroyo behind the camp: a hazard (DEX save DC 13 or 2d6 bludgeoning and swept away; Athletics DC 12 to pull someone out)

npcsInvolved.name: Tiburcio Archibeque, 17
npcsInvolved.role: Vaquero of the commons; the boy on the poster; the eyewitness
npcsInvolved.description: Slight, quick, black-haired, with a cowlick and a grin that hasn't been seen for a week. The best rider on the plaza. Nicanor's younger brother and Celestino's nephew. He took $20 to guide four horse buyers and saw a man killed.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To not be hanged, to not get his mother hurt, and, once he understands, to put the men who did it in front of a judge.

npcsInvolved.name: Rufina Sedillo, 38
npcsInvolved.role: Sheep owner of the commons; Tiburcio's protector; keeper of the act of possession (companion)
npcsInvolved.description: See her sheet. A widow who runs her late husband's two thousand sheep and his water rights, knows every arroyo of the commons, and has a paper in her wall.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To keep the springs open, the boy alive and her husband's honour, and to be listened to once.

npcsInvolved.name: Don Fermín Lucero, 61
npcsInvolved.role: The patrón; the Company's candidate for probate judge
npcsInvolved.description: Grey-bearded, straight-backed, courteous, in a black coat and a silver-buckled hat. Great-grandson of the founder, owner of sixty thousand sheep and a house of forty rooms. A Union officer of the New Mexico Volunteers in 1862. Proud of his name, his people and his bargain.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To save his people's houses and fields from a loss he thinks is coming anyway, and to keep the Lucero name honoured. He cannot bear to have been made a fool of, and he cannot bear to have made his people pay for it.

npcsInvolved.name: Doña Tomasa Lucero, 58
npcsInvolved.description: Small, plump, sharp-eyed, from a poor family of Los Ranchitos, married at sixteen. She has never liked the Company and has said so at every meal since March.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Her husband's soul, her granddaughter's happiness, and the plaza. She will help any party that is trying to save her husband from himself.

npcsInvolved.name: Ascensión 'Chona' Lucero, 19
npcsInvolved.description: Tall, quick, a fine horsewoman with a temper. In love with Rafael Candelaria, which her grandfather knows and pretends not to.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Rafael, the plaza and the truth, roughly in that order. She'll ride twenty miles to warn someone.

npcsInvolved.name: Don Policarpio Maestas, 78
npcsInvolved.role: President of the grant's comisión; keeper of the chest
npcsInvolved.description: Very old, white-haired, frail, with a clear mind and a little brass bell. He has been on the comisión since 1838. He keeps the church chest, which holds only an 1846 copy of the grant.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To pass the grant to his great-grandchildren whole, as he received it, and to keep the junta civil.

npcsInvolved.name: Don Crispín Maestas, 70
npcsInvolved.role: Herder at the Ojo del Gato; Don Policarpio's brother; a witness
npcsInvolved.description: Wiry, brown, toothless and fearless. He has watered his sheep at the stone tanks every morning for sixty years and tells the Company's guards so, daily.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To water his sheep, and to see the red-haired Texan hanged for what he did to Tiburcio.

npcsInvolved.name: Ozias Hornaday, 45
npcsInvolved.description: A thin, stooped, sunburned Ohioan with a theodolite, a demijohn and a conscience that keeps him awake. He moved the Cerro Colorado corner on Coldiron's instruction and knows exactly what it was worth.
npcsInvolved.motivation: His $150 a month and his professional name, which are now in conflict. Frightened enough, he'll tell a judge the truth to save the second.

npcsInvolved.name: Victoriano Romero, 44, of Laguna Pueblo
npcsInvolved.role: Section foreman at Paragon; Laguna's representative at the boundary
npcsInvolved.description: Compact, grey at the temples, dry and precise, in a railroad cap and a good wool coat. He speaks for his pueblo's governor and council on the matter of the corner. He is well respected by both towns and owes neither of them anything.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Laguna's boundary restored and Laguna's pasture left alone. He'll work with anyone who wants the same thing, and he will not be anybody's prop.

npcsInvolved.name: Thomasina Bevan, 41
npcsInvolved.role: Schoolmistress and chapel preacher at Plata Vieja; the miners' voice (companion)
npcsInvolved.description: See her sheet. Welsh, a miner's widow, square, plain-spoken and immovable.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To get the miners paid and their children fed, and to see that nobody, the Company or the plaza, treats three hundred and eighty men as cattle to be driven to a poll.

npcsInvolved.name: Venancio Chávez, 45
npcsInvolved.role: Owner of La Golondrina cantina; the People's precinct boss (companion)
npcsInvolved.description: See his sheet. He knows every vote on the plaza, and he owes the Company $600.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To win his precinct, as he has for twenty years, and to get out from under Rusk's letter without anyone finding out it exists.

npcsInvolved.name: Fenton Rusk, 50
npcsInvolved.description: As in st-scenario-001. Busy this week: the barbecue, the handbills, the letter to Venancio, the fence guards, and a quiet word with Rendell about Jethro Petree.
npcsInvolved.motivation: The election. He is beginning to worry about the party, and he will try to buy them before he tries anything else.

npcsInvolved.name: Cade Rendell, 38
npcsInvolved.description: As in st-scenario-001. In town he wears a white shirt and an ivory-handled revolver and leaves the buffalo rifle in its case at the Paragon House.
npcsInvolved.motivation: A showdown with a famous name in front of a crowd. Rusk wants him to wait. He's not good at waiting.

rewards.money: Nobody here has money, and the party should feel that. Rufina gives each party member a fat wether to sell or eat and the run of her camp. Don Fermín, if turned, offers the party $50 each, and is gravely hurt if they refuse and gravely pleased if they ask him to give it to the miners' children instead. Victoriano Romero gives nothing and promises nothing, and if trusted he keeps every promise he does make. Stolen notes bought back as evidence in Paragon cost a dollar each over face.
items: Tiburcio's sworn statement, taken down by Justice Lovato or Celestino (CLUE A5)
A copy, or the original, of the Paragon South Addition plat (CLUE E2)
Two or three stolen $10 notes from the Silver Rail (CLUE C2)
The Company's yellow handbill from Plata Vieja (CLUE D1)
The buckboard line's job letter to Jethro Petree (CLUE F3), and his confession, if he made it
Laguna's protest and Victoriano Romero's statement, if he trusts the party
The act of possession of 1768 (CLUE E5), in a tin box, in someone's keeping

twists: Rusk tries to buy the party before he tries anything else. On Tuesday or Wednesday he sends a note to wherever they are staying: a dinner at the Paragon House, and an offer of $200 each to 'help the Committee bring in the Archibeque boy, in safety, for a fair trial'. If they accept the dinner and not the money, he is charming, tells them nothing true, and learns whether they have the serial numbers. If they accept the money, the Company owns them, and Rendell knows it.

Celestino Trujillo's $300 from Hamish Gow is a bomb with a long fuse. If the party doesn't get to it first, the Paragon Pioneer prints it on Saturday 9 July under the headline 'THE PLAZA'S CANDIDATE BOUGHT BY THE MINE'. Celestino can defuse it by saying so first, at the junta or on the plaza on Saturday, with the receipt in his hand. He doesn't want to. He thinks it was nobody's business.

If Jethro Petree's confession is not taken on Wednesday night, he rides to Paragon on Thursday to beg Rusk to let him go. Rusk tells Rendell, and Jethro is the target on Sunday 10 July (st-scenario-003), a day earlier than he otherwise would be.

If Tiburcio is taken by the Committee, he is jailed in Paragon in Constable Ebner's lock-up behind the depot. A crowd begins to talk about the water tank, and st-scenario-003 opens with a jailbreak or a lynch mob instead of a rally. If he is hidden well, Rusk's riders keep looking, and the next place they look is the plaza jail.
dmTips: This scenario is the land: let the players feel what the commons are. Run at least one scene in Spanish, with translation by a companion, and let the vecinos argue with each other, not just with the Company.

Don Fermín is not a villain and should never be played as one. His argument at the junta is the best argument in the room on the evidence he has. The party turns him by showing him he has been deceived, not by beating him. When he breaks, give it time.
The fence is a trap for the vaqueros, and a good party sees it. A party that leads the fence-cutting anyway should win the fight and lose the newspapers. Make the cost visible on Friday morning.

Victoriano Romero represents his own nation's interest. Don't make him the plaza's ally, the party's guide or anyone's oracle. He knows the boundary because it is his pueblo's boundary, and he wants witnesses because his pueblo has learned what an unwitnessed boundary is worth. Do not give him or his companions any sacred practices or ceremonial lines; they are a section foreman and two elders on business.

Jethro Petree's confession is the most important scene in the scenario for the case, and the most fragile. Run it slowly. He's not a villain either. He's an old man who sold his friend for a job and a hundred dollars, and he knows exactly what he is.
The storm on Thursday is the season's first. From now on, every afternoon has a chance of thunder and flood (campaignRules, Coach and Road). Make the players feel the arroyos.

Budget an hour for the boy and the barbecue, an hour and a half for the fence, the junta and Jethro, and an hour for Thursday. If time is short, the Cerro Colorado can be told in a single scene on the way back from the sheep camp.
End on Friday with the news that Ludlow has sold the Puerco station, and with Rusk's next move, which the party may already guess: the repeaters arrive on the Saturday train.
